extracted.intended_audience: playwrights, comic poets, literary critics, and cultivated readers interested in the craft and evaluation of comedy
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative principles for composing and judging comic writing and stage comedy (esp. comedy of manners), drawing on historical examples (Moliere, Congreve, Shakespeare, Terence) to articulate what makes comedy 'good'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rarity and high standard of Good Comedies
rubrics_metrics.description: Good Comedies are such rare productions, that notwithstanding the wealth of our literature in the Comic element, it would not occupy us long to run over the English list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this as a baseline—expect that truly excellent comic works are uncommon and must survive rigorous tests; do not equate abundance of comic material with quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require a cultivated society and audience
rubrics_metrics.description: A society of cultivated men and women is required, wherein ideas are current and the perceptions quick, that he may be supplied with matter and an audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comedy that aims at the mind needs an audience with intellectual activity. Semi-barbarous, feverish, or highly unequal societies repel the great comic poet; consider audience sophistication when creating or staging comedy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subtlety and delicacy of the comic poet (natal gift)
rubrics_metrics.description: To touch and kindle the mind through laughter, demands more than sprightliness, a most subtle delicacy. That must be a natal gift in the Comic poet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comedy requires an innate subtlety—mere sprightliness or loud buffoonery won't achieve the intellectual aim. Cultivate precision of perception and refined touch rather than relying on coarse effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aim at the head (the mind), not merely the body
rubrics_metrics.description: People are ready to surrender themselves to witty thumps on the back, breast, and sides; all except the head: and it is there that he aims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Successful comedy addresses thought and understanding, not only physical mirth. Strive for laughter that provokes reflection rather than only momentary titillation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid catering to extremes (agelasts and hypergelasts)
rubrics_metrics.description: We have ... agelasts; that is to say, non-laughers ... and hypergelasts; the excessive laughers, ever-laughing ... Neither of these distinct divisions ... would be entertained by reading The Rape of the Lock, or seeing a performance of Le Tartuffe.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not tailor comedy exclusively to those who never laugh or to those who laugh at everything. Aim for a balanced audience; extremes distort the comic effect and appreciation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Position comedy at a 'middle distance' viewpoint
rubrics_metrics.description: We shall find ourselves about where the Comic spirit would place us, if we stand at middle distance between the inveterate opponents and the drum-and-fife supporters of Comedy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt a measured stance—neither sanctimonious moralism nor reckless licence. The best comic perspective observes and exposes without fanaticism or pandering.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comedy of Manners: avoid vacuous artificiality
rubrics_metrics.description: That fan is the flag and symbol of the society giving us our so-called Comedy of Manners, or Comedy of the manners of South-sea Islanders under city veneer; and as to Comic idea, vacuous as the mask without the face behind it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Don't produce characters who are mere painted puppets; the comedy of manners must have real human substance behind the manners, not merely surface types for easy laughs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Realism must be guided by idea; avoid raw realism
rubrics_metrics.description: Moliere ... did not paint in raw realism. He seized his characters firmly for the central purpose of the play, stamped them in the idea, and by slightly raising and softening the object of study ... generalized upon it so as to make it permanently human.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Realistic detail should be shaped and generalized to serve an underlying idea. Avoid slavish copy of life that lacks selection, elevation, or purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrate moral/idea organically into the work
rubrics_metrics.description: His moral does not hang like a tail, or preach from one character incessantly cocking an eye at the audience ... but is in the heart of his work, throbbing with every pulsation of an organic structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Moral or satirical purpose must be embedded in the play’s structure and character, not appended as didactic afterthought or stage-nodding aside.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wit should spring from reason and common-sense
rubrics_metrics.description: The source of his wit is clear reason: it is a fountain of that soil; and it springs to vindicate reason, common-sense, rightness and justice; for no vain purpose ever.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for wit that illuminates truth and supports ethical insight rather than sarcasm or cleverness for its own sake.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid ephemeral, empty, or merely 'rattling' wit
rubrics_metrics.description: Her wit is at once, like steam in an engine, the motive force and the warning whistle of her headlong course; and it vanishes like the track of steam when she has reached her terminus, never troubling the brains afterwards; a merit that it shares with good wine, to the joy of the Bacchanalians.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beware wit that produces momentary amusement but leaves no intellectual residue. The comic effect should be memorable and meaningful, not disposable sparkle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depth vs. prepared bon-mots (quality of wit)
rubrics_metrics.description: Congreve's wit ... is a surface wit, neither rising from a depth nor flowing from a spring. ... He drives the poor hack word, 'fool,' as cruelly to the market for wit as any of his competitors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer wit emerging organically from character and insight (Moliere) over pre-planned epigrams and contrived word-play that exist for their own dazzle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character must live in speech and presence (verisimilitude)
rubrics_metrics.description: It is a piece of genius in a writer to make a woman's manner of speech portray her. You feel sensible of her presence in every line of her speaking. ... There is a picturesqueness, as of Millamant and no other, in her voice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use voice, diction, and well-chosen detail to make characters vividly present on the page/stage; let manner of speech embody personality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comedy as social diagnosis and corrective
rubrics_metrics.description: The Femmes Savantes is a capital instance of the uses of comedy in teaching the world to understand what ails it. ... The farce of the Precieuses ridiculed and put a stop to the monstrous romantic jargon ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use comedy to expose and correct social absurdities and follies—when done well, comedy can change tastes and habits by revealing their ridiculousness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comedy must generalize to be permanently human
rubrics_metrics.description: He stamped them in the idea, and by slightly raising and softening the object of study ... generalized upon it so as to make it permanently human.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transform particular social types into broader human archetypes so the work transcends its moment and remains relevant to varied audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Need for lively social material (upper-class sparkle)
rubrics_metrics.description: Politically it is accounted a misfortune for France that her nobles thronged to the Court of Louis Quatorze. It was a boon to the comic poet. He had that lively quicksilver world ... under his eyes in full activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rich comedic material often comes from circles of extravagance and pretension; consider settings and social circles that provide contrast, pretension, and spectacle as fuel for comic situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role of women and comic empowerment
rubrics_metrics.description: Comedy is the fountain of sound sense; ... Comedy lifts women to a station offering them free play for their wit ... Dorine in the Tartuffe is common-sense incarnate ... Celimene is undisputed mistress of the same attribute in the Misanthrope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High comedy often gives prominent, intelligent roles to women—use female characters' wit and common sense as central comic forces rather than relegating them to passive prettiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Know the real world; do not expect too much of humanity
rubrics_metrics.description: To love Comedy you must know the real world, and know men and women well enough not to expect too much of them, though you may still hope for good.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A comic creator must be observant, realistic, and forgiving of human foibles; comedy demands accurate human knowledge tempered by humane hope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Idea (comic conception) over intricate plotting
rubrics_metrics.description: The fable is thin. The life of the comedy is in the idea.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritise a strong central idea or comic conceit rather than convoluted plotting; plots may be thin if the idea animates the characters and action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid jaded cynicism and heavy moralizing
rubrics_metrics.description: These bad traditions of Comedy ... are the ground of the heavy moralizings by which we are outwearied, about Life as a Comedy, and Comedy as a jade ... perversions of the idea of life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not let fatigue or cynicism produce shallow maxims or preachy moralizing; comedy should expose and correct, not merely sneer or moralize without insight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain purity of conception (comedy need not be impure)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Comedy of Moliere throws no infamous reflection upon life. It is deeply conceived, in the first place, and therefore it cannot be impure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High comic art can be morally clean while being incisive; impurity isn't a necessary component of effectiveness—aim for moral clarity and intellectual force.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simplicity and clarity of language
rubrics_metrics.description: He writes purely, in the simplest language, the simplest of French verse. The source of his wit is clear reason: it is a fountain of that soil; and it springs to vindicate reason ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer simple, precise language that serves clarity and reason; puns and verbal play should have semantic purpose, not only ornament.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wit as healing and vindication, not mere abuse
rubrics_metrics.description: When dead leaves and viler substances are heaped along the course, its natural song is heightened. ... It is full of healing, the wit of good breeding, the wit of wisdom.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use wit to remediate folly and restore common-sense, not merely to deride; let humor have restorative or corrective aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not pander to 'idle laughers' (popular low taste)
rubrics_metrics.description: Our traditions are unfortunate. The public taste is with the idle laughers, and still inclines to follow them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resist producing comedy that panders to base or instantly gratifying laughter; such pandering tends to corrode the idea and reduce longevity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal dignity and structural choices matter
rubrics_metrics.description: When she has frolicked through her five Acts to surprise you ... Five is dignity with a trailing robe; whereas one, two, or three Acts would be short skirts, and degrading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be deliberate about structure and form: act-length, pacing, and formal choices convey tone and dignity. Select the structure that best suits the nature and ambition of the comedy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innate disposition and temperament necessary for comic genius
rubrics_metrics.description: There are plain reasons why the Comic poet is not a frequent apparition; ... That must be a natal gift in the Comic poet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledge that some aspects of comic genius are innate; training helps, but certain temperamental gifts (subtle perception, balanced irony) are crucial and rarer than in other arts.
